$note: Written by hand, never generated. ExpressionTypingContractTests types every vector in its scope and grades the answer.

`scope` names an entry of `scopes`: `workflow` has node outputs, parameters, host namespaces, a helper and the clock; `outside` has only namespaces, a helper and the clock; `bare` has the clock alone, with no helper resolver.

A path holds its closed `term` and the `value` a run reads there; a namespace path is its key joined by dots. Outputs and parameters hold values in the CLR type of their term. A node output with `absent: true` has a term and no value: the run finds no such output.
A vector either has a `refusal` rule id (with `refusalCount` refusals when given, `position` of the first, and a fragment its message holds) or a result `term`.
`tree` is the preorder list of overload ids and conversions (`widen`, `to-text`, `convert`) the typed tree holds; every row of expression-functions.json occurs in one.
`value` is what the typed evaluator answers, inside `term`; `failure` is the category it throws instead. A vector with neither is typed and not evaluated.

`owner` is the task that provides the rule; the test grades the rows of dbc.10 and fails on an owner it does not know, so a later task adds its rows with its own owner and grader. dbc.10s adds the scopes declaring-item and declaring-value, which hold the variables an Expression<T> input declares.

bare.$note: no helper resolver and no namespace: ${helper.*} is expression-unknown-namespace

declaring-item.$note: the Expression<T> input that declares the variable item: Int; no other name is in scope

declaring-value.$note: the Expression<T> input that declares the variable value: String
